name: Esther

seo.title: Queen Esther: her story, her courage, Purim and her feast day
seo.description: Esther in plain words: the orphan who became queen of Persia, risked her life to save her people, her prayer, Purim, her feast day and the myths.

band.lede: An orphan raised by her cousin, she became queen of Persia. When a decree doomed her people, she went to the king unsummoned: “If I perish, I perish!”

She holds a letter. The background is dark.

who: Esther was a Jewish orphan in Persia, raised by her cousin Mordecai. She was taken into the palace of King Xerxes and made queen. When his chief minister, Haman, won a decree to wipe out her people, she risked death to plead with the king. She saved them. Jews still remember it every year at Purim.

tidbits.text: God is never named in the Hebrew book of Esther. Not once in ten chapters. The Greek text, read in Catholic and Orthodox Bibles, adds prayers that call on Him again and again.

cite.text: The book of Esther; Greek Esther 4, World English Bible

tidbits.text: The rabbis counted her among the prophetesses of Israel, and among “the four most beautiful women ever created.”
At Purim her book is read aloud from a scroll, and Haman's name is drowned out with noise. Some “wrote the name of Haman on the soles of their shoes” and stamped at every mention.

facts.label: In the Bible
facts.text: The book of **Esther**: ten chapters in Hebrew. **Catholic** and **Orthodox** Bibles read a longer **Greek** text, with her prayer and Mordecai's. Protestant Bibles follow the Hebrew.

facts.label: Home
facts.text: The citadel of **Susa**, the Persian capital, in what is now south-west **Iran**. Her family had been carried into exile from Jerusalem.

facts.label: Family
facts.text: An orphan, the daughter of **Abihail**, of the tribe of **Benjamin**. Her cousin **Mordecai** raised her as his own daughter. The Bible names no children.

facts.label: Her name
facts.text: **Hadassah** in Hebrew, which means **myrtle**. **Esther** is often taken to mean **star**.

facts.label: Her king
facts.text: **Xerxes** in the BSB, **Ahasuerus** in the Hebrew and many Bibles. The Greek text and Josephus call him **Artaxerxes**. Around 400, Sulpicius Severus confessed he could not easily tell which king it was.

facts.label: Also called
facts.text: **Queen Esther**. **Righteous Esther**, in the Orthodox Church. The Fathers saw in her a figure of the **Virgin Mary**, the *Catholic Encyclopedia* says.

facts.label: Died
facts.text: The Bible does not say. Jewish tradition puts her tomb at **Hamadan**, the ancient Ecbatana, in Iran, beside Mordecai's.

facts.label: Her feast
facts.text: **Purim**, on 14 and 15 **Adar**, in February or March. Jews still keep it, and read her book from a scroll.

facts.label: In art
facts.text: Painters often chose the scene from the Greek text where she **faints** before the king, as Artemisia Gentileschi did on this page.

feasts.note: The **Orthodox** keep her on a Sunday, not a date. The **OCA** names **Righteous Esther** on the **Sunday before the Nativity**, between 18 and 24 December. The **Catholic** and **Anglican** calendars have no day for her. Jews remember her every year at **Purim**.

quotes.q: Esther also, being perfect in faith, exposed herself to no less danger, in order to deliver the twelve tribes of Israel from impending destruction. For with fasting and humiliation she entreated the everlasting God, Who seeth all things; and He, perceiving the humility of her spirit, delivered the people for whose sake she had encountered peril.
quotes.who: Clement of Rome, writing to the church at Corinth, about 96

cite.text: Clement of Rome, Letter to the Corinthians, chapter 55

quotes.q: Why did Queen Esther expose herself to death and not fear the wrath of a fierce king? Was it not to save her people from death, an act both seemly and virtuous?
quotes.who: Ambrose of Milan, teaching his clergy about what is right

cite.text: Ambrose, On the Duties of the Clergy, Book 3, chapter 21

quotes.q: There was a certain Hebrew woman, Esther was her name. This Esther rescued the whole people of the Jews, when they were about to be delivered over to destruction, by this very method.
quotes.who: John Chrysostom, in Antioch in 387, while its bishop went to plead with the emperor for the city. The method he meant was prayer.

moments.title: An orphan in Susa
moments.text: Mordecai, a Jew of the tribe of Benjamin, lived in the citadel of Susa. He had brought up his uncle's daughter, Hadassah, that is Esther, “because she did not have a father or mother.” When her parents died, he took her as his own daughter. The young woman “was lovely in form and appearance.” Before this, Queen Vashti had refused to come when the king sent for her to show off her beauty to his guests. The king had put her away, and now he sent out a search for a new queen.

moments.title: Queen in Vashti's place
moments.text: Young women were gathered from every province, and “Esther was also taken to the palace.” Hegai, the eunuch in charge of the women, favoured her. At Mordecai's word, she told no one who her people were. Each woman had twelve months of beauty treatments before her night with the king. When Esther's turn came, she asked for nothing but what Hegai advised. “And the king loved Esther more than all the other women.” He set the royal crown on her head and made her queen.

moments.title: A plot against the king
moments.text: Two of the king's eunuchs plotted to assassinate him. Mordecai, sitting at the king's gate, learned of it. “He reported it to Queen Esther, and she informed the king on Mordecai's behalf.” The plot was confirmed, and both men were hanged. It was all written in the king's chronicles, and nothing was done for Mordecai. Not yet.

moments.title: Haman's decree
moments.text: The king raised Haman the Agagite above all his princes, and commanded everyone at the gate to bow to him. Mordecai would not. In a rage, Haman set out to destroy not Mordecai alone but all his people. The Pur, the lot, was cast to choose the day: the thirteenth of Adar. Haman offered ten thousand talents of silver to the treasury, and letters went out to every province “to destroy, kill, and annihilate all the Jews.” “Then the king and Haman sat down to drink, but the city of Susa was in confusion.”

moments.title: For such a time as this
moments.text: Mordecai tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and wailed through the city. Esther sent him clothes, but he would not take them. Through the eunuch Hathach he sent her a copy of the decree and urged her to plead with the king. She reminded him of the law: anyone who went in to the king unsummoned would die, unless he held out his gold scepter. And she had not been called for thirty days. Mordecai sent back: “Do not imagine that because you are in the king's palace you alone will escape the fate of all the Jews.” And then: “Who knows if perhaps you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this?” Her answer is below, in her words.

moments.when: The third day of the fast
moments.title: The gold scepter
moments.text: On the third day, Esther put on her royal robes and stood in the inner court, facing the king's throne. “She found favor in his sight.” He held out the gold scepter, and she came near and touched its tip. “What is your request?” he asked. “Even up to half the kingdom, it will be given to you.” She asked only that the king and Haman come to a banquet she had prepared. At the banquet he asked again. Again she asked only for another banquet, the next day.

moments.title: A sleepless night
moments.text: Haman went home glad, until he passed Mordecai at the gate, who would not rise for him. His wife Zeresh and his friends told him to build a gallows fifty cubits high and ask to have Mordecai hanged on it. “That night sleep escaped the king.” He had the chronicles read to him, and heard how Mordecai had saved his life. Nothing had been done for him. In the morning Haman came to ask for Mordecai's death, and the king asked him, “What should be done for the man whom the king is delighted to honor?” Haman, sure it was himself, proposed a royal robe and a royal horse. Then he had to lead Mordecai through the city square in them.

moments.title: The second banquet
moments.text: At the second banquet the king asked a third time: “Queen Esther, what is your petition?” Now she answered. She asked for her life and her people's, for they had been “sold out to destruction, death, and annihilation.” The king asked who had dared. Esther named him to his face. The king rose in fury and went out into the garden. Haman fell on the queen's couch to beg for his life, just as the king came back. A eunuch mentioned the gallows at Haman's house. “Hang him on it!” said the king. So Haman was hanged on the gallows he had built for Mordecai.

moments.title: Letters to undo the decree
moments.text: That same day the king gave Esther Haman's estate, and she told him who Mordecai was to her. Mordecai received the king's signet ring. Then Esther fell at the king's feet and wept, begging him to undo Haman's evil plan. A decree sealed with the king's ring could not be revoked. So Mordecai wrote new letters in the king's name, allowing the Jews in every city to assemble and defend themselves on the day set for their death. He went out in royal robes of blue and white. “For the Jews it was a time of light and gladness, of joy and honor.”

moments.title: The days of Purim
moments.text: On the day their enemies had hoped to overpower them, “their plan was overturned and the Jews overpowered those who hated them.” When the king told Esther of the dead in Susa and asked what more she wanted, she asked that the Jews of Susa have one more day, and that the bodies of Haman's ten sons be hanged on the gallows. Then came rest, feasting and gifts to the poor. Mordecai sent letters to keep the feast of Purim, named for Haman's lot, every year. Queen Esther wrote too, “with full authority,” and “Esther's decree confirmed these regulations about Purim.” It is the last the Bible tells of her.

words.note: Esther wrote no book. Her words are kept in the book that bears her name. Outside the quiz's own section, every Bible line on this page is from the Berean Standard Bible. The lines from the Greek text, which only Catholic and Orthodox Bibles hold, are from the World English Bible.

feature.kicker: To Mordecai, before she went in to the king
feature.q: After that, I will go to the king, even though it is against the law. And if I perish, I perish!
feature.ctx: Mordecai had warned her that silence would not save her. She sent back word to gather the Jews of Susa and fast for her three days, “night or day,” while she and her maidens fasted too.

quotes.q: The adversary and enemy is this wicked man—Haman!

quotes.q: O my Lord, You alone are our King. Help me. I am destitute, and have no helper but You, for my danger is near at hand.

myths.claim: Esther said, “For such a time as this.”
myths.truth: Mordecai said it, in a message sent to her: “And who knows if perhaps you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this?” Her own answer was a fast of three days, and “If I perish, I perish!”

The book tells of no contest she chose to enter. The king's commissioners gathered young women from every province into his harem, and “Esther was also taken to the palace.” Each had twelve months of beauty treatments, then one night with the king. Esther asked for nothing but what Hegai advised. The king loved her more than all the others and made her queen.

The Hebrew says she was “the daughter of his uncle,” which makes them cousins. Josephus calls Mordecai her uncle, and many retellings follow him. Either way, Mordecai raised her “as his own daughter.”

circle.name: Mordecai
circle.text: Her cousin, who raised her as his own daughter. He would not bow to Haman, and he ended second only to the king.

circle.name: King Xerxes
circle.text: Her husband, called Ahasuerus in many Bibles. He loved Esther more than all the other women, and three times offered her up to half his kingdom.

circle.name: Haman
circle.text: The Agagite the king raised above all his princes. He plotted to destroy her people, and was hanged on the gallows he had built for Mordecai.

circle.name: Vashti
circle.text: The queen before her, put away for refusing to come at the king's command.

circle.name: Hegai
circle.text: The king's eunuch in charge of the women. Esther pleased him, and when her turn came she took only what he advised.

circle.name: Hathach
circle.text: The king's eunuch appointed to her. He carried her messages to Mordecai, and Mordecai's back to her.

saint.big: The Orthodox honour her as **Righteous Esther** on the Sunday before Christmas, among the righteous of the Old Testament. Lutherans of the Missouri Synod keep her day on 24 May. The Catholic calendar has no day for her.

prayer.title: Her prayer
prayer.intro: In the Greek text of her book, kept in Catholic and Orthodox Bibles, Esther prays through the three days of the fast. She takes off her royal robes, puts on mourning and covers her head with ashes. The lion in her prayer is the king.
prayer.q: Remember us, O Lord! Manifest Yourself in the time of our affliction. Encourage me, O King of gods, and ruler of all dominion! Put harmonious speech into my mouth before the lion … But deliver us by Your hand, and help me who am alone and have no one but You, O Lord.

kin.name: Joseph
kin.text: Raised high at a foreign court, he too saved his people. He told his brothers, “it was to save lives that God sent me before you.”
